newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on China talk, delivery ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on China talk, delivery ideas.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower as China exported more corn and on ideas for increased deliveries on the March contract, traders said.

"Malaysia bought corn from China and that was the key here," said Jason Roose, analyst with U.S. Commodities. "China and Argentina are going to compete with our export lineup so that's putting pressure on the corn market."

Position squaring was noted before expiration Wednesday at 1201 CST of the March contract. The open interest in that contract, at roughly 24 million bushels early Tuesday, was considered a bit lofty before an expiration day.

The amount of corn registered with the CBOT for potential delivery increased 310,000 bushels Tuesday and as of late Tuesday totaled 1,035,000 bushels. That hike in registrations led to prospects for increased deliveries on the March.
Corn closed two to 5-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 4-1/4 at $3.06. May closed 5-3/4 cents per bushel lower at $3.01.
New crop December corn gained over two cents per bushel relative to the nearby May.
"Some people were buying the new crop because they want to talk about flooding," said Paul Haugens of FIMAT Futures.

The U.S. Commerce Department Tuesday forecast the most widespread spring flooding in the U.S. in a decade. That possibility continued to limit selling interest in new crop contracts because of concerns about delays in seeding the crop.
Technicians early Tuesday cited first support in the May at $3.02-1/2 and second support at $2.96. The session low for May was $3.00.
First resistance was at $3.09-1/2 and second resistance was at $3.16. The session high for the May was $$3.04-3/4.
Chartists said the four- and 20-day moving averages for the May early Tuesday were giving off bullish signals.
The short term nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the May closed at 52.8 percent. The market considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 78,000 contracts, below the 90,122 traded Monday.

Cargill Inc sold 4.5 million bushels of July, Refco Inc sold six million July and sold 2.5 million December, traders said. Prudential Securities sold 2.5 million July and LIT America sold 1.5 million May, traders said.
Smith Barney bought six million bushels of July. Also, Smith Barney bought 3.5 million December, traders said. LFG bought four million bushels of May, traders said.

In corn options, Prudential Securities bought 300 May $3.10 calls and bought 300 May $3.10 puts at 22 cents, traders said. Tenco Inc bought 200 May $2.90 puts and sold 200 May $3.20 calls at 1/2 cent, sold 300 May $2.90 calls at 17 centsand sold 300 May $3.10 calls at 7-1/2 cents.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, about in line with the 12,437 traded Monday.
